core_concept: Markets have distinct session boundaries (Asia 00-07, pre-London 07-08, London 08-13, overlap 13-16, NY 16-21 UTC). Each transition resets inventory, changes volatility, and shifts participation.
foundational_rule: Always anchor trade decisions to session time and inventory state. Pre-London low volume differs fundamentally from London open breakout.
why_matters: Session-aware trading exploits predictable volatility and inventory resets. Ignoring session structure leads to trades on low-conviction setups.

core_concept: Tick volume (number of trades, not contract volume) drops during Asian session due to low participation. Spikes indicate participation change. Overnight inventory either resets (Asia) or carries forward (London→NY).
foundational_rule: Low tick volume = thin market, wide spreads, vulnerable stops. High tick volume = acceptance, directional conviction. Never short-scalp thin volumes.
why_matters: Tick volume predicts spread quality and slippage. Trading thin volume setups wastes edge to commissions and slippage.

core_concept: A swing high requires: (1) bar closes above prior two bars, (2) next bar(s) fail to exceed it, (3) reversal candle pattern confirms. Swing low mirrors this inversely.
foundational_rule: Do not trade pivots until confirmed. A potential pivot that breaks on the next bar was never a pivot—it was just a local extreme.
why_matters: Unconfirmed pivots are noise. Confirmed pivots are valid reversal zones with defined invalidation (if price exceeds pivot on new attempt).

principle_name: Higher Highs / Higher Lows Trend Definition
core_concept: Uptrend = 5+ consecutive bars where each swing high > prior swing high AND each swing low > prior swing low. Downtrend mirrors inversely. No trend = HH/LL pattern breaks.
foundational_rule: Trend direction is always-in. If bar closes above prior swing high, bias is long until proven otherwise. If bar closes below prior swing low, bias is short.
why_matters: Trend bias eliminates second-guessing. The setup (reversal candle, pullback, breakout) only matters if aligned with trend direction. Counter-trend setups have lower conviction.

core_concept: When a prior support level is broken decisively and price returns to that level, it becomes resistance (role reversal). The level no longer attracts buyers; it now attracts sellers.
foundational_rule: Trade role reversals at the break level on the retest. Stop above the reversal level (opposite of support logic). Target is the next lower swing low.
why_matters: Role reversals have high conviction because they mark a fundamental shift in market structure. Support/resistance are not fixed; they flip when broken.

core_concept: Measured move = (swing_end − swing_start) × multiplier + breakout_level. Typically 1.0x distance. E.g., if swing is 100 pips, expect 100-pip move from breakout.
foundational_rule: Use measured move as target, not as entry signal. Entry comes from separate setup (breakout, pullback, candle pattern). Measure move targets are zones to watch, not guarantees.
why_matters: Measured moves exploit momentum imbalance. When a level breaks, market often extends by the prior swing distance before pausing.

core_concept: Bullish engulfing: prior candle body fully inside current candle, current closes above prior close. Bearish mirrors inversely. Must occur at pivot or after failed breakout.
foundational_rule: Engulfing patterns are valid only at extremes (pivot highs, pivot lows, broken levels). In middle of trend, they are noise.
why_matters: Engulfing patterns show absorbed selling/buying. Price rejected prior direction and absorbed all of it. High conviction at extremes.

core_concept: Doji = open ≈ close (< 5% of bar range) with long wicks. Signals indecision. At swing extremes, doji precedes reversal. In trends, doji = temporary pause.
foundational_rule: Doji at swing high/low + follow-through bar = reversal trade. Doji in middle of trend = skip it. Doji must be at an extreme to matter.
why_matters: Doji show market cannot decide a direction. At extremes, this indecision flips into reversal. In trends, it's just retracement noise.

principle_name: Piercing Line & Dark Cloud Cover: 50% Penetration
core_concept: Piercing line: bearish candle, next candle opens low but closes > 50% into prior body (bullish). Dark cloud inverse (opens high, closes < 50% into prior body). Both require context at extreme.
foundational_rule: Penetration depth matters. > 50% = strong signal. < 30% = weak signal. Always confirm with next bar before entering.
why_matters: Penetration patterns show rejection of prior direction. The deeper the penetration, the stronger the rejection. 50% is the threshold between weak and strong.

core_concept: HTF (higher timeframe) bar has three states: (1) Developing (not yet closed), (2) Closed above prior close, (3) Closed below prior close. LTF action during developing state reveals HTF momentum.
foundational_rule: Never enter LTF trades if HTF bar is developing and approaching a level. Wait for HTF close. HTF state > LTF noise.
why_matters: HTF bar development is the market structure. LTF details are secondary. Trading against HTF development is like swimming upstream.

core_concept: Triple screen = HTF trend direction + MTF trend direction + LTF reversal signal. All three aligned = highest conviction. 2 of 3 = medium. 1 of 3 = skip.
foundational_rule: Entry requires HTF trend up, MTF trend up, AND LTF reversal bullish. If HTF is down, skip all long entries regardless of LTF signals.
why_matters: Timeframe alignment filters noise. LTF signals work 3× better when aligned with HTF direction. Misalignment = false signals.

core_concept: Break hierarchy: LTF breaks before MTF before HTF. If LTF breaks a level but MTF level not yet broken, await MTF confirmation before aggressive entry.
foundational_rule: LTF break alone = setup candidate. MTF confirmation = entry signal. HTF confirmation = conviction multiplier.
why_matters: Incomplete breaks are false signals. Waiting for next-level confirmation avoids early entries that reverse before gaining ground.

core_concept: After a swing, LTF pullback that retraces 50-61.8% of HTF swing distance is optimal entry zone. < 38% = weak pullback. > 78% = too deep (trend reversal risk).
foundational_rule: Enter pullbacks at 50-61.8% Fib level with stop below the level. If pullback exceeds 78%, trend has reversed—flip to reversal entry.
why_matters: Fibonacci levels are natural retracement zones. 50-61.8% gives best risk/reward: far enough from trend start to confirm trend, close enough to pullback zone.

core_concept: If price is stretched > 2 ATR from moving average, market is overextended. Trend continues but pullback likelihood is high. Skip trend entries at extreme stretch.
foundational_rule: If price > 2 ATR from MA: skip new trend entries, await pullback. If price < 0.5 ATR from MA: entry zone, trend likely to extend.
why_matters: Overextension predicts pullback. Entering at extreme stretch has poor risk/reward (small target before pullback, large stop needed).

core_concept: Liquidity sweep = price takes out swing extreme (capturing stops) then reverses sharply. Often happens at session open or news event. Swing extreme is 'baited' then reversed.
foundational_rule: When swing extreme is taken, expect reversal within 2-3 bars. Enter reversal after first pullback bar following the sweep. Stop above sweep level.
why_matters: Sweeps are deliberate. Market breaks extremes to capture stops, then reverses. Recognizing this pattern avoids being stopped out.

principle_name: Order Block: Prior Swing Bar as Support/Resistance
core_concept: Order block = the swing bar that preceded a reversal. On retest, order block bar acts as support/resistance. Rejection at order block signals reversal continuation.
foundational_rule: When price retests order block zone (±5 pips of order block), watch for rejection. Rejection candle at order block = high conviction reversal entry.
why_matters: Order blocks mark where prior reversal occurred. Retesting them shows market is revisiting the decision point. Rejection = confirmation.

principle_name: Fair Value Gap (FVG): Candle Range Gap
core_concept: FVG = gap between prior candle's close and next candle's open (no bar overlap). Also called imbalance. FVG persistence > 20 bars = strong, indicates unfilled demand/supply.
foundational_rule: FVG within 5 bars of formation can be broken and closed. FVG aged 20+ bars is strong—breakout or breakdown from FVG is high conviction.
why_matters: FVGs are market memory. Unfilled gaps are inefficiency. Market revisits and fills them eventually, but aged gaps show strong directional bias.

principle_name: Gap Classification: Breakaway vs Measuring vs Exhaustion
core_concept: Breakaway gap = first gap in trend, large body, close at extreme end. Measuring gap = middle of trend, similar size to prior gaps. Exhaustion gap = late trend, small body, potential reversal.
foundational_rule: Breakaway gap signals trend start, ride it. Measuring gap = continuation, extend position. Exhaustion gap = reduce/exit, reversal coming.
why_matters: Gap type predicts trend continuation or reversal. Early gaps mean trend has room; late gaps mean exhaustion. Position sizing should reflect gap type.

core_concept: Thin band = price range < 0.5 ATR over 3+ bars. Signals compression. After compression, expect expansion (trend breakout or reversal).
foundational_rule: Thin band = setup stage. Await band break. Do not fade within band. Break of band edge = high conviction entry.
why_matters: Thin bands are accumulation/distribution. Price is gathering strength before move. Breaking band boundary releases that energy.

core_concept: Spike-channel = sharp rise/fall followed by parallel channel. Upper band = resistance, lower band = support. Price oscillates between bands while maintaining trend direction.
foundational_rule: Enter long at lower band within spike-channel trend. Stop below lower band. Target = upper band or beyond. Exit if channel breaks.
why_matters: Spike-channels are reliable trends with defined edges. Trading the edges (lower band long, upper band short) has high win rate.

core_concept: 20-bar MA = trend anchor. Price oscillating around MA = healthy trend. Price breaks MA decisively = trend reversal. Price touches MA = support/resistance to trade.
foundational_rule: Bullish trend: buy pullbacks to MA. Stops below MA. If price closes below MA for 3+ bars, trend reversal in progress.
why_matters: MA is the simplest, most reliable trend filter. It removes noise and shows true trend direction. Respects it; violate it only on strong reversals.

principle_name: Trend Break: Consecutive Closes Below Swing Low
core_concept: Uptrend ends when 2+ consecutive bars close below most recent swing low. Downtrend ends when 2+ consecutive bars close above most recent swing high.
foundational_rule: Trend break = reversal signal. Enter reversal after first bar post-break closes below swing. Stop above swing low. Ride reversal until new trend establishes.
why_matters: Trend break is objective, mechanical, and high conviction. It marks exact moment uptrend became downtrend (or vice versa).

principle_name: Climax Veto: Volume Spike with No Follow-Through
core_concept: Climax = extreme volume bar at trend extreme with no follow-through next bar. Signals trend exhaustion. Market made its move; reversal likely.
foundational_rule: If high volume bar with large body appears at swing high/low with no follow-through bar: skip trend entries, prepare reversal setup.
why_matters: Volume climax shows aggressive intent (one side took control) that immediately failed. This failure signals reversal, not continuation.

core_concept: Range = price oscillates between high (resistance) and low (support) for 10+ bars without trending. Two-sided trading. No directional bias.
foundational_rule: In range: fade edges (short near high, long near low). Targets = opposite edge. Stops = 3-5 pips beyond edge. Avoid directional trades.
why_matters: Ranges exploit mean reversion. Price moves away from edge, then reverts. Trading edges in ranges has predictable risk/reward.

principle_name: Range Expansion: Breakout of Both Edges
core_concept: Range expansion = price breaks both high and low edges. Signals trend initiation from range. Usually follows range compression phase.
foundational_rule: Entry when price breaks first edge on volume. Confirm on second break. Target = prior swing or measured move. Stop inside range.
why_matters: Range expansion ends two-sided trading and initiates trend. It's one of highest conviction breakout setups because range acted as confirmation zone.

principle_name: False Breakout: Break + Reversal Within N Bars
core_concept: False breakout = price breaks edge decisively, then closes back inside range within 3-5 bars. Signals weakness in breakout direction.
foundational_rule: After false breakout: expect range continuation or reversal in opposite direction. Avoid chasing initial breakout; wait for fade back into range.
why_matters: False breakouts trap directional traders. Recognizing them early avoids being caught on wrong side of reversal.

principle_name: Barbwire Pattern: Consecutive Reversals at Edge
core_concept: Barbwire = 2+ consecutive hammer/hanging man candles at same range edge. Signals edge rejection. Stop placement here is vulnerable to breakout.
foundational_rule: When barbwire appears: fade edge with tight 3pip stops. If stop hit, expect breakout next. Do not use barbwire edge as stop location.
why_matters: Barbwire is wicked: price probes edge, reverses (hammer), probes again (another hammer). It looks like rejection but can suddenly break. Requires tight stops.

core_concept: Open above range = bullish bias (likely to fill gap to top). Open below range = bearish bias. Open inside range = neutral (could go either way).
foundational_rule: Open bias: use it as directional hint. Open above high → long bias until proven false. Open below low → short bias. Revise if price breaks opposite edge.
why_matters: Open location shows overnight overnight sentiment and inventory. It's a free signal of likely day direction if range holds.

core_concept: MTR = (1) trend break below/above swing, (2) retest of broken swing level (holds = confirmation), (3) second entry bar in new direction. Three-bar pattern.
foundational_rule: Step 1: Trend break (2+ consecutive closes). Step 2: Retest (price returns to break level, holds without breaking it again). Step 3: Enter second bar post-hold. Stop above/below hold level.
why_matters: MTR is mechanical and high conviction. Each step filters false signals. By step 3, reversal is confirmed with low false-positive rate.

principle_name: Failure Test: Retest That Fails to Reach Level
core_concept: Failure test = broken level is retested but fails to reach it (stops short), then reverses. Price does not exceed break level on retest.
foundational_rule: When retest stops short of broken level: enter reversal immediately. Stop 5pips above/below retest low/high (opposite of break level). High conviction.
why_matters: Failure test is definitive reversal confirmation. Price had chance to return to broken level but couldn't. This weakness signals strong reversal.

core_concept: BRG = (1) swing breaks, (2) price retraces back to break level (within 5pips), (3) reverses away ("go"). Three-bar entry pattern.
foundational_rule: Entry: third bar after retrace completes (the 'go' bar). Stop: 5pips on opposite side of retrace. Target: prior swing or measured move.
why_matters: BRG is mechanical, easy to spot, and high conviction. It's the most reliable reversal entry pattern with defined entry/stop/target.

principle_name: Bounce Rejection: Failed Bounce into Old Trend
core_concept: Post-reversal bounce = brief movement back into old trend direction. Rejection = that bounce is stopped sharply and reverses again. Signals reversal strength.
foundational_rule: After trend break, if bounce into old trend is rejected sharply: add to reversal position. Bounce rejection = confirmation, not weakness.
why_matters: Bounce rejection shows market tried to recover trend but couldn't. Double-confirmation of reversal. Opportunity to increase position size.

principle_name: Two-Bar Reversal: Extreme Bar + Reversal Bar
core_concept: Two-bar reversal = (1) extreme bar (high close or low close at extreme), (2) next bar reverses sharply (low bar after high, high bar after low).
foundational_rule: Entry: second bar of pattern, on close. Stop: 5pips opposite extreme. Target: opposite swing or measured move.
why_matters: Two-bar reversal is simplest mechanical pattern. No confirmation needed. Extreme exhaustion visible in bar 1; reversal starts bar 2.

principle_name: Session Opening Reversals: London & NY Overlap
core_concept: London open (08:00 UTC): overnight trend often reverses on London participation. NY overlap (13:00-16:00 UTC): trend reversal as NY enters overlapping with London.
foundational_rule: 30 min before/after session open: watch for reversals. If overnight trend reverses on session open: high conviction reversal setup.
why_matters: Session participation shifts cause inventory rebalancing. New session buyers/sellers can overwhelm prior sentiment. Opening reversals are statistically reliable.

principle_name: Deep Pullback Discrimination: > 50% as Continuation Risk
core_concept: Post-reversal pullback > 50% of reversal swing = deep. Deep pullbacks risk reversal failing (original trend resuming). Shallow pullback < 38% = lower risk.
foundational_rule: If pullback > 50%: assess if reversal is real. Check for reversal bars, MA hold, or failure test. Pullback > 78% = original trend resuming (not reversal).
why_matters: Deep pullbacks test reversal conviction. If reversal can't hold shallow pullback, it's false. Shallow pullback = reversal strength confirmed.
